clue.text: Race without losers for one of these political groups

definitions.text: Race without losers for one of these political groups

parts.words: Race without losers for one of these political groups
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Dodo organises a race in which everybody wins and all get prizes, named after a kind of party meeting

explanation.surface: A political note about an election contest in which nobody is allowed to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's caucus-race has no losers: everyone runs in circles and all win. The clue asks for the plural of the political meeting that gives that race its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a closed meeting of party members choosing candidates or policy; the plural names several such groups.

clue.text: Means the girl Inside is getting old

indicators.note: inside tells us the girl's name goes within the word for getting old

parts.note: ages as a verb means grows old
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A remark that the girl indoors is beginning to look her age.
explanation.definitionFit: Averages are arithmetic means, the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: Structure to study for atom in fission

parts.note: con is an old word for study or learn

indicators.note: fission splits the atom, so these letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A scientist studies the make-up of an atom being split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the anagram fodder with 'atom', and 'fission' is the anagram signal; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Conformation is the shape or arrangement of parts, as of a molecule or an animal's body.

clue.text: Postpones trouble hoisting this at sea

parts.note: stays means delays or postpones, as in a stay of execution
ail means trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sailor puts off hoisting a sail because it is giving trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A staysail is a triangular sail set on a stay, raised on a ship.

clue.text: Silent bird on the water on Welsh coast

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the bird comes before the water

parts.note: the mute swan is a bird known for being silent
the sea is the water

explanation.surface: A mute swan floats on the sea off the coast of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a port city by the sea in south Wales.

clue.text: Quick, alter the poster !

indicators.note: alter tells us to change the order of the letters of poster

explanation.surface: An urgent order to change a poster at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction for a very fast tempo.

clue.text: Style of decoration sound, I see

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British decoration

indicators.note: sound tells us the following word is taken as heard, as a single letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like C

explanation.surface: Someone admires a sound decorating style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but signals that 'see' is said aloud as the letter C. CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish elegance, fashionable smartness.

clue.text: Show him clemency — he's a standby for the play

definitions.text: he's a standby for the play

explanation.surface: An understudy who is pardoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is an instruction to show mercy to a man; as a phrase it is an extra player kept in reserve for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparing a man is showing mercy; a spare man is a reserve player ready to step in.

clue.text: Staff dance in factory building

parts.note: the works can mean the workforce employed at a plant
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: The employees hold a dance inside their factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, joining the wordplay to the definition rather than putting one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop is a room or shed within a plant where things are made or repaired.

clue.text: Audible performance of bird

indicators.note: audible tells us the word for performance is to be taken as heard, then respelt

parts.note: a turn is a single act or performance in a variety show

explanation.surface: Someone praises a bird's song as a fine show to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: The tern is a slender seabird with forked tail, related to the gull.

clue.text: Space traveller's evidence of a tea-time poltergeist

explanation.surface: A spaceman offers proof that a ghost has been throwing the crockery at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a UFO; the second takes the phrase literally, a piece of tableware sailing through the air thrown by a mischievous spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a supposed alien spacecraft and a dish under a cup hurled across the room by a ghost fit the phrase.

clue.text: Do they subscribe to their own policies ?

definitions.text: Do they subscribe to their own policies ?

parts.words: Do they subscribe to their own policies ?
parts.note: subscribe means literally sign underneath; insurers sign beneath the policies they issue, taking on the risk

explanation.surface: Asks whether people agree with their own principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policies' seems to mean beliefs, but these are insurance policies, and 'subscribe' means sign beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers who accept liability by signing beneath an insurance contract.

clue.text: Lady counsellor — a wildly eager one

indicators.note: wildly tells us to throw the letters of these words about into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A female adviser who is extremely keen.
explanation.walkthrough: Egeria was the nymph who advised Numa, the legendary king of Rome; her name now means any woman adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeria, the nymph who guided King Numa, gave her name to any female adviser or patroness.

clue.text: Beginning late to blame that's about right

parts.note: ex means former, as late can mean former

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for blame wraps around the letter for right

parts.note: odium is hatred or disgrace attached to someone, blame

explanation.surface: Someone says it is right to start blaming those who arrive late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like a word about time, but here it means former, as in 'the late chairman'; 'about' signals that one piece wraps around the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: An exordium is the opening part of a speech or treatise, its introduction.

clue.text: Say, Lulu is in a muddle generally

indicators.note: in a muddle tells us the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A girl called Lulu is, as a rule, confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally and as a rule are synonyms for what happens most of the time.

clue.text: Taken to bits and getting no place

explanation.surface: A dismantled thing that is left out of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Stitching that is unpicked is taken apart; a player not chosen for a side is also unpicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstitched or dismantled; and not selected for a team.

clue.text: Shady character of a region in Italy ?

explanation.surface: A sinister figure turns out to come from an Italian province.
explanation.walkthrough: Umbra is Latin for shade, so the word reads as having the nature of shadow; it also means from Umbria, a region of central Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from Umbria in central Italy, and by a play on umbra (shadow) shadowy in nature.

clue.text: Foul to link me, a Greek character, with backward citizen

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: backward tells us the short word for citizen is written in reverse

parts.note: cit is an old short form for a citizen, a townsman

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it foul to be linked with a Greek and a slow-witted townsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like an insult to the citizen but reverses CIT into TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephitic describes a foul-smelling, noxious gas or vapour.

clue.text: But German river north of northern UK city

indicators.note: in a down clue north of means placed above, so these letters come before the next

parts.note: aber is the German word for but
the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales

explanation.surface: A geographic note about a German river lying north of a northern British city.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdeen indeed stands on the river Dee, so the geography of the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland, part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Bathe in stormy sea? Nothing in it, Fatty!

indicators.note: in tells us the dip goes inside the shuffled sea
stormy tells us the letters of sea are tossed about

parts.note: a dip is a short bathe
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A plump swimmer is mocked for taking a dip in a rough sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'Noth-in it', with the end of 'Nothing' lost at the line break. 'stormy' signals the anagram of the water's three letters, and 'in' puts the bathe and the zero inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means of or consisting of fat, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Fairy dropped and died

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite of Persian legend
shed means let fall, as a tree drops its leaves

explanation.surface: A fairy fell to the ground and expired.
explanation.definitionFit: Perished is a synonym for passed away, often from cold or hardship.

clue.text: Took note as he destroyed deed

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the letters of the words are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone paid attention as a man tore up a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention to advice or warning.

clue.text: Wool-worker comes a cropper

explanation.surface: A knitter takes a heavy fall.
explanation.walkthrough: One who purls (a knitting stitch) is a wool-worker; 'come a purler' is British slang for falling headlong, like 'come a cropper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone knitting the purl stitch; and a headlong fall, British slang equal to taking a tumble.

clue.text: Polyphony as opposing argument

parts.note: counter means against or opposing
a point is an argument made in debate

explanation.surface: A musician likens several voices at once to a debate between rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterpoint is music made of several independent melodic lines played together.

clue.text: It's taken as the standard of the regiment

explanation.surface: A regiment's flag is held up as its emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a regimental flag; it is a standard quantity of measurement, and a regiment is itself a military body of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed quantity used in measuring; and a military formation such as a regiment.

clue.text: Oriental study of Paradise

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: An eastern scholar's room is a heavenly place.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden where Adam and Eve lived, a byword for a perfect place.

clue.text: Dress tie ruined by woman running press

indicators.note: ruined tells us the letters of the two words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's formal tie is spoilt by a woman using an iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like ironing, the surface's picture; it means a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a female editor, the one in charge of a publication.

clue.text: Covering directions to accountant to sign perhaps

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
N is north, another compass direction
CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: perhaps tells us the word may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Cover instructions are sent to the accountant, maybe for signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosing something in a box or sheath is wrapping or covering it.
